name: showreel-33-carousel

voice.text: Why does your carousel stop between photos? Your swipe stops where your finger lets go: half of two photos. The fix: scroll snap type, x mandatory, and snap align, center. Now every swipe lands on one whole photo.

caption:
Why does your carousel stop between photos? 📸

A row of photos with overflow-x: auto scrolls freely, so it stops wherever your finger lets go: half of one photo, half of the next. Add scroll-snap-type: x mandatory to the row and scroll-snap-align: center to each photo, and every swipe settles on one whole photo. No JavaScript, no library. Works in Chrome 69+, Safari 11+ and Firefox 99+.
Save it for your next product gallery, or send it to whoever built your carousel.

sources.note: MDN scroll-snap-type: set on a scroll container; mandatory = the viewport must snap to a snap position when it is not being scrolled; BCD: Chrome 69, Firefox 99 (68-98 partial), Safari 11 (iOS 11)
MDN scroll-snap-align: the box's snap position (start, end, center) within its snap area; BCD: Chrome 69, Firefox 68, Safari 11

tip.title: Why does your carousel stop between photos?
tip.why: A scrolling row stops wherever the finger lets go, so a swipe often ends on half of two photos. scroll-snap-type: x mandatory on the row makes it settle on a snap position every time, and scroll-snap-align: center on each photo makes that position the photo's centre (MDN). No JavaScript.
